ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The MOS band diagram shows the metal on the left, the SiO2 oxide in the middle, and the semiconductor on the right. The oxide-semiconductor interface is the right vertical boundary of the SiO2 layer. In the semiconductor, the labeled bands EC, Ei, and EV bend strongly near the surface/interface and then become nearly flat farther into the bulk. The dotted EFS line is approximately horizontal through the semiconductor. In the bulk region, EFS lies above Ei, indicating an n-type bulk. Near the surface, the band bending raises Ei relative to EFS so that the surface condition corresponds to the opposite carrier type from the bulk. Therefore, the surface region is in inversion.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the oxide-semiconductor interface and trace the labeled EC, Ei, EV, and EFS curves from the surface into the bulk. Then compare EFS with Ei in the bulk and at the surface. Since the band bending makes the surface carrier type opposite to that of the bulk semiconductor, classify the surface condition as inversion.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct band-diagram classification route: determine carrier type from the relative positions of the semiconductor Fermi level and intrinsic level at the bulk and at the surface, then identify inversion when they indicate opposite carrier types.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the MOS band diagram: metal on the left, SiO2 oxide barrier, semiconductor bands EC, Ei, and EV on the right. Note that in the bulk region on the far right, EFS lies above Ei, while near the oxide/semiconductor surface the band bending places the intrinsic level relative to EFS in the opposite sense, indicating a reversal of majority carrier character at the surface.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know that the required blank is the operating condition of the MOS surface region shown by the band diagram.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the MOS rule that the sign and magnitude of band bending are interpreted by comparing EFS with Ei. If the surface carrier type is opposite to the substrate/bulk carrier type, the surface is in inversion.
